title: Integer and units endpoint squares for etale-to-pro-etale pullback
statement: Let f : X → Y be an arbitrary morphism of schemes. Use the inverse images and comparison morphism of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] and [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], the integer comparison of [def-sp-tower-class-reduction], and the units comparison of [def-sfb-cartier-reduction-data]. Write V = nu_Y^*, W = nu_X^*, P = f_proet^*, Q = f_et^*, and kappa : V ⋙ P ≅ Q ⋙ W for comparisonUpperStarCompUpperStarIso. Let iY : V(Z_Y,et) ≅ Z_Y,proet and iX : W(Z_X,et) ≅ Z_X,proet be integerComparison. Let z : P(Z_Y,proet) → Z_X,proet be adjoint to the constant-section map and zEt : Z_X,et → Q(Z_Y,et) be the inverse constant-sheaf comparison. Let bY and bX be cartierUnitsComparison and bEt : Q(G_m,Y,et) → G_m,X,et the adjoint units comparison. For any a : P(G_m,Y,proet) → G_m,X,proet whose adjoint pulls every unit on every chart U back along U ×_Y X → U, the following two equalities hold: P(iY.inv) ≫ kappa.hom_Z = z ≫ iX.inv ≫ W(zEt), and kappa.inv_Gm ≫ P(bY) ≫ a = W(bEt) ≫ bX. These are equalities of sheaf morphisms, before taking cohomology or towers.

source.place: Paragraph (2), integral class change of site and its canonical units maps; Stacks Tag 00WX for inverse-image adjunctions

proof.text: For integers, transpose through the two composite inverse-image adjunctions and the constant-sheaf adjunction. The site comparison kappa is the mate of the canonical direct-image square. integerComparison is the unique comparison of the constant-sheaf left adjoints. Its definition and that of upperStarConstantSheafIso identify both transposes with the section map k ↦ constant(k) on the base-changed chart. Injectivity of the adjunction hom equivalences proves the first equality.

For units, transpose through the same two composite inverse-image adjunctions. cartierUnitsComparison transposes to identity on the units of each etale chart. The hypothesis about a and the definition of upperStarGmSheafToGmSheaf both transpose to pullback of the unit along the fibre-product projection. The base-change isomorphism defining the direct-image square commutes with the first projection, so these maps agree. By injectivity of the adjunction hom equivalences this proves the second equality.

theorem integral_site_pullback_endpoints {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (a : (upperStar AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} f).obj (Scheme.proEtaleUnitsSheaf Y) ⟶
      Scheme.proEtaleUnitsSheaf X)
    (ha : ∀ (U : Y.ProEtᵒᵖ) (x : (Scheme.proEtaleUnitsSheaf Y).obj.obj U),
      (((upperStarLowerStarAdjunction AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} f).homEquiv _ _) a).hom.app
          U x =
        ULift.up (Additive.ofMul
          (Units.map (pullback.fst U.unop.hom f).appTop.hom.toMonoidHom x.down.toMul))) :
    let κ := comparisonUpperStarCompUpperStarIso AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} f
    let z := ((upperStarLowerStarAdjunction AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} f).homEquiv _ _).symm
      (Scheme.proEtaleConstantDirectImageMap f AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}
        (AddCommGrpCat.of (ULift.{u + 1} ℤ)))
    let zEt := ((Scheme.upperStarConstantSheafIso AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} f).symm.app
      (AddCommGrpCat.of (ULift.{u + 1} ℤ))).hom
    ((upperStar AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} f).map (integerComparison Y).inv ≫
        κ.hom.app ((constantSheaf Y.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}).obj
          (AddCommGrpCat.of (ULift.{u + 1} ℤ))) =
      z ≫ (integerComparison X).inv ≫
        (comparisonUpperStar AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} X).map zEt) ∧
    (κ.inv.app Y.gmSheaf ≫
        (upperStar AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} f).map (cartierUnitsComparison Y) ≫ a =
      (comparisonUpperStar AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} X).map
          (Scheme.upperStarGmSheafToGmSheaf f) ≫ cartierUnitsComparison X)
